title: Deleting the last visible text item in the clipboard applet clears the clipboard regardless of its non-text contents
line: Deleting the last text entry in the Clipboard popup no longer wipes an image you copied afterwards.
explanation: With 'save images' off (the default), Klipper skips copied images without noting that the clipboard now holds something that isn't in the history. When the history became empty (last entry deleted) it cleared every buffer not holding a password, and when the top entry was deleted it wrote the next entry over the buffers, so the image was lost either way. The change tracks per buffer that it holds skipped data, exactly like the existing password tracking, and leaves those buffers alone; picking an entry or copying something new clears the mark as before.

commits.message:
klipper: keep images that are not saved when deleting history entries

With images not saved, the history didn't know a copied image was in the
clipboard, so deleting the last entry cleared it. Now buffers holding
skipped images are tracked like passwords and left alone in that case.

BUG: 452287

media.caption: Master: after clicking the trash button on 'texto-A' the clipboard is empty, the image is gone.
With the fix: after deleting 'texto-A' the clipboard still holds the image.

review.text: Fixes the actual cause in HistoryModel: skipped images were not tracked, so emptying the history or deleting the top entry overwrote the buffer. Mirroring the existing per-buffer password tracking is the natural, minimal approach and the flag is cleared on every new copy, pick or empty clipboard. Verification covers the bug and the top-entry variant. Minor: clearHasPassword() now also clears the unsaved flags, so its name is slightly misleading.
